title: Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Twenty-second Dynasty — also called the Bubastite or Libyan dynasty — was founded around 943 BC by Shoshenq I, a Meshwesh Libyan chieftain who seized the throne from the weak Twenty-first Dynasty and ruled from Bubastis and Tanis. Shoshenq I is almost certainly the biblical 'Shishak' who sacked Jerusalem around 925 BC, as recorded in both 1 Kings 14 and his victory relief at Karnak. The dynasty's apogee came under Osorkon II (c. 872–837 BC), after which the kingdom fragmented as competing Libyan warlords established rival dynasties in the Delta, reducing pharaonic authority to a patchwork of city-states. Osorkon IV, the dynasty's last ruler, was displaced around 716 BC by the Nubian pharaoh Piye of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Nile Delta and Upper Egypt territories are moderately well-attested through Egyptian administrative records, but the patchwork nature of late-dynasty political control means any single polygon overstates coherent sovereignty.
